description: Network resources that cost money and serve nothing, next to look-alikes that do serve something. An Elastic IP attached to nothing, a NAT gateway no used route table points to, an internet-facing load balancer whose only target group is empty, and two servers whose public IPs nothing can reach and which cannot send out through them either (one auto-assigned, one an Elastic IP). Not flagged: a web server the internet reaches, a server that uses its public IP only to send out, and the NAT gateway the private subnets use. Two per-gigabyte costs are reported for checking: a private subnet that reaches S3 through the NAT gateway with no gateway endpoint, and a subnet in us-east-1b whose NAT gateway is in us-east-1a (its route table already has the S3 endpoint).
